title: [Chapitre] VII. Analysis situs (troisième mouture) : notes manuscrites (23-26/06/1986).

deep.reconstruction:
Context: this is page 54 of the 1986 'Analysis situs' notes. There Grothendieck axiomatizes a point-free geometry of 'figures', called an 'atelier' (workshop). An atelier is A = (F, ≤, ≪): F is a set of figures, ≤ is the subfigure order, and ≪ is a 'well inside / strictly interior' relation. From these he derives two further relations. ∥ means 'disjoint / separated'. The negated ≷ (written ≹, '#') means roughly 'in general position / compatible'; 'x ≹ y' is read here as 'x and y are compatible'. The 'lieux' L are the minimal elements, playing the role of points. M is used for a class of figures (elements, or 'cells'). For a figure X, omb(X), its 'ombre' or shadow, is the set of points x ≪ X. Fig(L) is the concrete atelier of figures on the point set L. The canonical comorphism is φ: F → Fig(L), F ↦ mulomb(F), the shadow of F with its induced figure structure.

The page returns to 'set-theoretic ateliers', meaning ateliers realised by subsets of a point set. These come in two kinds: 'spacieux' (any two compatible figures have their union as a figure) and 'polyédral' (the previous page adds the axiom that bounded pairs have an infimum).

Proposition: compare two conditions.
(i) φ is an embedding of ateliers (cf. GF VI p.51) and its image is a spacious sub-atelier. Concretely:
- (a) for every F, F' ↦ φ(F') gives a bijection Ssfig(F) → Ssfig(φ(F)) of subfigures ('stricte');
- (b) φ(F) ≪ φ(G) ⇒ F ≪ G, hence φ is injective;
- (c) φ(F) ≹ φ(G) ⇒ F ≹ G.
(ii) F is spacious in the absolute sense (one of the four equivalent axiom systems of p.45: AtL1, AtL2, AtL3, AtCL(spac)), and distinct points are separated: x ≠ y ⇒ x # y.
He claims (i) ⇒ (ii). He also notes that (ii) gives (i a) and (i c) but not (i b).

Proof begun here:
- Distinct points have distinct singleton images φ(x), φ(y), which are compatible in Fig(L). By (c), x ≹ y.
- AtL1 (every figure X has a point below it, 'divisibility'): X ≠ ∅ implies φ(X) ≠ ∅, i.e. omb(X) is nonempty.
The next page does AtL2 and AtCL, and starts the converse via Lemma 1: for a dense subset Λ, φ_Λ is strict.

In modern terms this is a representation theorem. It characterises when an abstract point-free structure of regions is isomorphic to a concrete structure of point-sets on its 'points'. It is the analogue of 'a locale is spatial iff it has enough points', or of Stone/de Vries-type representation of region/contact algebras. It serves Grothendieck's programme of a foundation of tame ('modérée') topology that starts from figures rather than points.
errors: Notation drifts between L (lieux/points) and M (the class of figures being tested). AtL1 is stated for X ∈ M although the statement of (ii) is phrased via L.

The remark '(ii) ⇒ (ia) (mais pas (ib) vu l'injectivité de φ)' is garbled. It is unclear which implications are claimed. The final architecture (both directions, which parts of (i) are recovered from (ii)) is only settled on the next page, and the stated 'Alors (i) ⇒ (ii)' is just one direction.
The step 'φ(x), φ(y) ponctual figures, hence compatible' relies on the convention that distinct singletons in Fig(L) are ≹. This is true in the concrete model but not justified on the page.
The AtL1 proof is essentially a definitional unwinding. AtL1 is only nontrivial once one knows φ(X) ≠ ∅ for X ≠ ∅, which itself uses injectivity (b) and φ(∅) = ∅. That step is left implicit.

ideas.what: Abstract 'atelier' (F, ≤, ≪) of figures with derived disjointness ∥ and compatibility relations, as a point-free foundation for tame topology
ideas.modern_name: region-based / point-free topology; contact (proximity) algebras, mereotopology; locales
ideas.usually_credited_to: de Vries (1962) compingent algebras; Whitehead/Tarski region-based geometry; Isbell/Johnstone locales; Düntsch–Vakarelov contact algebras
ideas.where_published: Only the general wish for 'topologie modérée' is in Esquisse d'un programme (1984); ateliers appear only in these unpublished Analysis situs notes

ideas.what: Canonical comorphism F ↦ shadow (set of points well inside F) into the concrete atelier Fig(L), and a criterion for it to be an embedding with spacious image
ideas.modern_name: spatiality / representation theorem ('enough points'), analogous to Stone and de Vries duality
ideas.usually_credited_to: Stone (1936); Isbell, Johnstone (spatial locales); de Vries (1962)

ideas.what: Separation axiom: distinct points are disjoint/separated (x ≠ y ⇒ x # y), forcing AtL3
ideas.modern_name: T1/Hausdorff-type separation of points in point-free setting

missed.claim: Grothendieck's ateliers, with a well-inside relation ≪, disjointness ∥ and a representation of figures by shadows on minimal 'lieux', are structurally a theory of contact/proximity (de Vries/mereotopological) algebras. They are adapted to polyhedral and tame figures, with a spatiality criterion. This link between his tame-topology programme and region-based topology / de Vries duality seems not to have been made in the literature.
missed.quote: Soit A=(F,≤,≪) un atelier, considérons le (co)morphisme canonique φ : F → Fig(L), F ↦ Mulomb(F)
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Point-free foundations of o-minimal/tame geometry, and region-based theories of space, could benefit from Grothendieck's axioms (spacieux vs polyédral, AtL1–3, divisibility).

missed.claim: The equivalence (i) ⇔ (ii) characterising set-theoretic ('spacieux') ateliers is only partially proved. The polyhedral analogue announced at the top of the page ('soit polyédral') is not treated here.
missed.quote: Ce sera un atelier soit spacieux, soit polyédral, pour nous les premiers cas.
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: A complete representation theorem for polyhedral ateliers would give an axiomatic characterisation of polyhedral/tame figure-systems.

deep.surprise_reason: The atelier axiomatics and this representation criterion are unpublished and fit a point-free tame-topology programme. The mathematics itself is a natural spatiality/representation lemma, close to known locale and contact-algebra results.
transcription_corrections: 'Malomb(F)' should almost certainly read 'Mulomb(F)' (multiplicité-ombre), consistent with 'mul omb_Λ(F)' on p.55.
The relation written '≸ / ≷' with a slash is Grothendieck's negated-comparability/compatibility symbol (≹). The '#' in 'x # y' is likely the same or the ∥ sign.
The crossed-out word before 'figures ponctuelles' is probably 'fermées' rather than 'fermables'.
'loc cit p. 40' refers to the definition of spacious sub-atelier in GF VI.
